info.title: Yabane API
info.description: Yabane is a transparent LLM gateway. Inference endpoints proxy OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Anthropic Messages to configured Providers. OpenAI Responses can explicitly target a ChatGPT Plus/Pro OAuth subscription Endpoint. Control endpoints manage Providers, Endpoints, Provider credentials, model routes, gateway access, and activity. Every action available in the web console is available here.

gatewayKey.description: Gateway API key (sk-…) for inference endpoints. Provider scopes apply.

managementKey.description: Management API key (yab_mgmt_…) for control endpoints.

ModelPricing.description: Explicit USD rates per million tokens. Input and output must both be available after Endpoint, Provider, and Global field inheritance before Yabane can estimate cost. Within one scope, an exact model pattern wins; otherwise the longest matching prefix ending in one '*' wins. Across scopes, the narrower scope supplies the rate, field by field. No Provider type, Endpoint URL, model name, or built-in catalog supplies an implicit price.

cache_write_per_million.description: Reserved for compatibility. Current normalized usage has no cache-write token count, so estimation does not apply this rate.

updated_at.description: Unix timestamp set by Yabane when the effective table is saved.

models.description: Outgoing rules: exact model IDs Yabane sends to the Provider, or non-empty prefixes ending in one '*', mapped to rates. These prices win over incoming rules for the same request. An empty map clears this part of the scope.

incoming_models.description: Incoming rules: exact model names callers send, including public routing aliases, or non-empty prefixes ending in one '*', mapped to rates. Supported only by Global pricing, because a caller-facing name belongs to no single connection. One rule covers every destination whose model has no outgoing price. The same pattern may not appear in both maps of one table, and patterns must not start or end with whitespace.

EndpointView.description: A Provider Endpoint, including the words and sign-in flows its Endpoint type declares. Tokens and account IDs are never included.

api_type.description: Endpoint type identifier, either one Core implements or one an Extension declares.

pricing.description: Outgoing overrides for exact or trailing-wildcard Provider model patterns; omitted fields inherit from the selected Provider and Global rules, and these rules win over a Global rule for the caller-facing name.

endpoint_type_label.description: Present when an Extension owns this Endpoint type: the Endpoint type's own name.

fixed_base_url.description: Present when the Endpoint type fixes the base URL, in which case only the proxy and rate-limit policy can be edited in place.

sign_in.description: Present when the Endpoint type connects accounts through its own sign-in flow.

enabled.description: Whether this Extension executes Hooks or provides its Endpoint implementation in the current process.

runtime_configurable.description: False when --no-extensions prevents runtime enablement for this process.

endpoint_types.description: Endpoint types this Extension declares; an Extension that declares none leaves this empty.

PricingSource.description: The configured pricing rule behind one effective rate.

pattern.description: The matching key in that scope's pricing table.

name.description: Whether the rule matched the model name the caller sent or the model ID Yabane sent to the Provider.

gateway_api_key_id.description: Stable ID of the authenticated Yabane Gateway API key. Null when authentication was disabled or for records created before this metadata was introduced.

gateway_api_key_note.description: Safe display note captured from the Gateway API key at request time. The secret and secret hash are never recorded.

gateway_api_key_prefix.description: Non-secret display prefix of the authenticated Gateway API key.

model.description: Model string exactly as supplied by the caller.

upstream_model.description: Exact model ID selected by routing and placed in the request to the Provider. Null for records created before this metadata was introduced.

upstream_credential_id.description: Stable ID of the Endpoint credential that carried the request. Null for Endpoints without credentials and for records created before this metadata was introduced. Provider secrets are never recorded.

upstream_credential_name.description: Name the Endpoint credential had when it carried the request, so the record stays readable after the credential is deleted or when it is read on an instance that does not configure it. Null for Endpoints without credentials and for records created before this metadata was introduced. Credential material is never recorded.

credential_cooling.description: Whether the identity that carried the request was itself cooling down at selection time, because the Endpoint had no eligible identity left or a model route pinned an exhausted one. False for Endpoints without credentials and for older records.

route_mode.description: Selection mode of the model route that chose the destination. Null when no model route matched and the caller's Provider/model ID was used directly.

route_priority.description: Priority group of the destination that carried the request. Null unless a failover route chose it.

route_failover.description: Whether the destination was taken while a lower-numbered group could not serve because every destination in it was cooling down.

status.description: Final proxy outcome. Streaming protocol-conversion failures are recorded as 502 even when HTTP response headers were sent before the failure was detected.

failure.description: Structured, safe diagnosis for a failed proxied request. It does not contain credentials, prompt or response content, Provider URLs, proxy addresses, or untrusted Provider error text.

latency_ms.description: Total elapsed milliseconds from request arrival until the proxied response completes.

gateway_ms.description: Milliseconds spent reading, routing, and preparing the request before starting the Provider request. Null for records created before timing breakdowns were introduced.

upstream_response_ms.description: Milliseconds from starting the Provider request until its response headers arrive.

first_byte_ms.description: Milliseconds from request arrival until the first Provider response-body chunk is observed; unavailable when no body chunk is observed.

generation_ms.description: Milliseconds from the first observed response-body chunk until response completion.

cost.description: Provider-reported cost when available, otherwise an estimate from explicit pricing; null when neither is available.

pricing_sources.description: Which configured rule supplied each estimated rate, so an estimate stays explainable after pricing changes. Written only for estimated costs.

cost_source.description: Origin of cost. Older records with cost but no source are interpreted as reported.

finish_reason.description: Terminal reason or status reported by the Provider protocol. OpenAI Chat Completions uses finish_reason, Anthropic Messages uses stop_reason, and OpenAI Responses uses incomplete_details.reason or its terminal status. Null when unavailable or for older records.

upstream_streaming.description: Whether the Provider response itself streamed. Only a streamed response has a generation phase to time, so throughput and first-token averages are aggregated from these records instead of being inferred from the caller's streaming preference. False for older records.

source_instance_id.description: Originating instance for imported records; omitted for records created by this instance.

priced_requests.description: Requests with either Provider-reported or explicitly estimated cost.

latency_ms.description: Total latency across all matching requests.

by_model.description: Per-model totals grouped by the requested model_dimension: the incoming name by default, otherwise the model ID sent to the Provider, with an empty name for requests that recorded none.

by_api_key.description: Request and usage statistics grouped by stable Gateway API key identity. Legacy and authentication-disabled traffic is grouped as Unattributed.

provider_buckets.description: Request counts for each Provider using the same ordered intervals as buckets.

filter_options.description: Available Provider, exact requested-model, and safe Gateway API-key values from the selected time range before dimension filters are applied.

id.description: Stable Gateway API key ID, or __unattributed__ for traffic without an attributed key.

requests.description: Request count in each interval; its length matches buckets.

priced_requests.description: Requests in this dimension with reported or estimated cost.
Requests in this interval with reported or estimated cost.

input.description: Input tokens reported for this interval.

output.description: Output tokens reported for this interval.

latency.description: Sum of end-to-end latency in milliseconds across samples.

first_byte.description: Sum of first-byte latency in milliseconds over first_byte_samples.

first_byte_samples.description: Successful requests whose Provider response streamed, so a first byte could be timed.

generation.description: Sum of generation time in milliseconds after the first byte over generation_samples.

generation_tokens.description: Output tokens generated during generation time; divide it by generation to read throughput as a measured ratio.

generation_samples.description: Successful streamed responses with a positive measured generation time.

TrafficCaptureConfig.description: When active, provider_id and endpoint_id are required together and expires_at must be a future Unix timestamp.

dropped.description: Captures or configuration updates dropped because the bounded queue was full or persistence failed.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds from beginning observation of the final Provider request until the exchange completed. Null for captures retained before this field was introduced.

TrafficCaptureRecord.description: Credential-redacted Provider request and response headers and bounded body byte arrays.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed milliseconds from beginning observation of the final Provider request until the exchange completed.

CredentialView.description: An identity Yabane uses when sending a request to a Provider, described with the vocabulary of the Endpoint type that declares its kind. Secrets, refresh tokens, and account IDs are never included.

id.description: Stable within its Endpoint; model-route destinations refer to it.

priority.description: Priority group, lowest first. Traffic uses the lowest-numbered group that still has an eligible identity, so a higher-numbered group carries nothing while a preferred identity can serve. Configuration written before priorities existed is one group.

kind.description: Identity kind identifier declared by this Endpoint's type.

subscription_expires_at.description: Present for OpenAI subscription credentials; the access token renews automatically shortly before this time.

cooldown_seconds_remaining.description: Present only while the credential is cooling down after a Provider rate-limit response.

kind_label.description: How this Endpoint's type names one identity of this kind.

RateLimitCooldown.description: Explicit policy that turns a 429 from the Provider for one credential into a cooldown during which that credential is not selected. The configured length is the ceiling in every mode: a cooldown never outlasts it.

seconds.description: 0 disables the policy. Otherwise the longest a credential can stay out of selection after the Provider answers 429, in seconds.

mode.description: Where the length of the cooldown comes from. fixed uses seconds and ignores anything the Provider reports. prefer_provider uses the Provider's own Retry-After when it carries an integer number of seconds, and seconds when it does not. provider_only uses the Provider's own delay and arms no cooldown when there is none, so a rate limit without a usable delay changes nothing.

RateLimitCooldownActivity.description: What an Endpoint's cooldown policy has done since this process started, including the delay the Provider's own answer asked for when it armed the most recent cooldown. Present on an Endpoint only while its policy is enabled, so a policy that can be configured correctly and still never fire is distinguishable from a working one.

applied.description: How many 429 answers selected a cooldown duration, including a reported zero-second delay that starts no new cooldown.

skipped.description: How many 429 answers from the Provider carried no usable delay under a policy that requires one, and therefore changed nothing.

last_seconds.description: How long the most recent applied cooldown lasted, in seconds.

last_reported_seconds.description: The delay the Provider's own answer asked for, in integer seconds. Zero is a reported delay, not a missing value. Absent when the answer carried no delay Yabane reads. Recorded even under fixed, which does not use it to choose the duration.

last_source.description: Why the most recent delay was selected at response time: fixed configured duration, unchanged Provider delay (including zero), Provider delay capped by the configured maximum, or configured maximum used because no delay was reported. Later policy edits do not reinterpret this observation. Absent before any delay has been selected.

last_applied_at.description: Unix timestamp of the most recent applied cooldown. This is runtime state and is not persisted: it resets when the process restarts.

last_observed_at.description: Unix timestamp of the most recent 429 answer observed on this Endpoint, whether it armed a cooldown or changed nothing. Runtime state, reset on restart.

CredentialKindView.description: One identity kind declared by an Endpoint type. The Endpoint type owns this identifier, its label, and whether it holds a pasted secret or a signed-in account.

id.description: Identifier persisted with each credential of this kind.

label.description: How this Endpoint type names one identity, for example its console wording.

flow.description: `secret` identities carry a pasted secret; `subscription` identities carry a signed-in account's tokens and expiry.

EndpointTypeSignIn.description: Sign-in flows this Endpoint type offers. Address sign-in requests by Endpoint type, not by Provider.

EndpointTypeView.description: An Endpoint type this process can offer: one Core implements, or one a compiled and enabled Extension declares. Core never infers these properties from the identifier.

default_endpoint_id.description: Suggested Endpoint ID for a new Endpoint of this type.

fixed_base_url.description: Present when the declaration fixes the base URL, in which case the connection cannot be edited in place.

native.description: True when Core implements this Endpoint type rather than an Extension.

ExtensionEndpointTypeView.description: An Endpoint type this Extension declares. Configured Endpoints of this type become unavailable while the Extension is disabled.

EndpointSignInState.description: Progress of one Endpoint-type sign-in. Device-code fields are present for the device-code flow; the browser flow exposes its authorization URL instead. Tokens, authorization codes, and PKCE verifiers are never returned.

Conflict.description: The request is understood but conflicts with the current state of another resource.

InternalServerError.description: Yabane could not complete the operation.

post.summary: Proxy OpenAI Chat Completions
post.description: The model field selects routing: provider/model, or a public model route alias. Yabane prefers a native Chat Completions Endpoint and otherwise converts the request and successful response to the configured Provider protocol; conversion is reported in the response header and Activity. Cross-protocol conversion preserves exact JSON tool-argument strings between OpenAI surfaces and uses target-specific stop, parallel-tool and content-part shapes. Inline files sent to Anthropic need an explicit MIME type, normally via a base64 data URI; unsupported file content returns 400 rather than disappearing. Refusal reasons remain visible; malformed or divergent converted streams fail instead of returning an empty successful answer.

post.summary: Proxy OpenAI Responses
post.description: Yabane prefers a native Responses Endpoint and otherwise converts the request and successful response to the configured Provider protocol. ChatGPT Plus/Pro subscription Endpoints require stream=true when calling the Provider and use the explicitly configured Codex backend adapter. Cross-protocol requests with non-null previous_response_id or conversation return 400; supply full input history instead. Generic conversion omits provider-specific reasoning and groups assistant text within a tool-call batch so results remain adjacent. Native Responses history is forwarded unchanged.

post.summary: Proxy Anthropic Messages
post.description: Yabane prefers a native Anthropic Messages Endpoint and otherwise converts the request and successful response to the configured Provider protocol; native paths remain transparent. Generic cross-protocol conversion omits thinking and redacted_thinking history because Anthropic signatures are not portable OpenAI encrypted reasoning.

Both maps are cleared together when they are empty, and patterns must not start or end with whitespace; no built-in prices are restored.

post.summary: Create or replace a public model route
post.description: Every target must currently be usable. Validation and persistence are serialized with Provider and Endpoint mutations so a concurrent deletion cannot leave a dangling target. An OpenAI subscription target requires the OpenAI Subscription Extension to be enabled; disabling it later retains the route but makes that target fail visibly until re-enabled. A failover route is validated and described in its own mode's terms: priority groups of at least 1, one 100% split per group, and a destination that cannot serve being reported rather than skipped.

pattern.description: Exact model ID or one trailing * wildcard.

mode.description: weighted gives every enabled destination its configured share whether or not its identities are cooling down. failover groups destinations by priority: the lowest-numbered group with a destination that still has an identity to use carries the traffic, and a group is left only while every destination in it is cooling down. A destination whose configuration cannot serve is never skipped, so a standby group cannot hide it.

weight.description: Traffic percentage. A 0% share disables the destination. A weighted route's shares must total 100; a failover route's must total 100 inside each priority group.

enabled.description: Optional compatibility field. False sets the target's effective share to 0; a 0% weight is always inactive.

credential_id.description: Optional credential ID to pin. Omit or use an empty string to keep the Endpoint credential policy, which selects among enabled credentials and skips ones that are cooling down. A pinned credential is always used exactly as configured.

priority.description: Priority group for a failover route, lowest first. A weighted route stores but never reads it.

patch.description: Replaces the route identified by the current pattern. The request may also change the public pattern. Every target must currently be usable, including having any Endpoint implementation Extension enabled, and validation is serialized with Provider and Endpoint mutations.

post.summary: Recalculate non-reported Activity costs
post.description: Recalculates existing estimated costs and fills missing costs using the current explicit Global, Provider, and Endpoint pricing. Outgoing rules win over a Global incoming rule, and a record without a Provider model ID can still be priced through the name the caller sent. Provider-reported costs and legacy costs without a cost_source are preserved. An optional request_id limits the operation to one Activity record; source_instance_id disambiguates imported records that share a request ID.

request_id.description: Stable request ID. When omitted, every retained non-reported record is considered.

source_instance_id.description: Source Activity instance ID for an imported record. Omit it with request_id to select a record created by this Yabane instance.

Traffic uses the lowest-numbered group that still has an eligible identity, so a higher-numbered group carries nothing while a preferred identity can serve. patch.summary: Update a Provider credential name, weight, priority group, or enabled state
patch.description: Updates any subset of the credential name, weight, and enabled state without replacing its secret. Renaming keeps the stable credential ID, so model-route destinations and historical records continue to refer to the same identity.

name.description: Display name for the credential. Whitespace-only names are rejected with 400.

enabled.description: A credential pinned by a retained model-route target cannot be disabled until that target is updated or deleted.

priority.description: Move this identity to another priority group. Percentages are read within a group, so the traffic distribution of the groups it leaves and joins has to be updated to total 100 again.

delete.description: Returns a cooling credential to selection immediately. Health is runtime state only, so restarting Yabane forgets every cooldown as well.

delete.summary: Delete an API endpoint and its route destinations

patch.description: Updates an Endpoint and its connection settings without exposing or replacing existing API-key secrets or Endpoint request defaults. Changing id atomically updates current discovered-model availability, model Endpoint preferences, model-route destinations, Provider Request Defaults scope, and an inactive Traffic Capture scope; historical Activity and retained captures keep the ID recorded when each request occurred. An active Traffic Capture scoped to the Endpoint must first be stopped. Disabling required authentication atomically clears credential references from model-route targets. Enabling it is rejected while keyless route targets still refer to the Endpoint. OpenAI subscription Endpoints accept ID and SOCKS5 proxy changes only; their API type, base URL, and credential requirement remain fixed.

id.description: The desired unique Endpoint ID. Changing it updates current configuration references.

patch.summary: Set traffic distribution across enabled endpoint credentials within each priority group
patch.description: Set one positive integer percentage for every enabled credential. Percentages must total 100. Credentials that hit a configured rate-limit cooldown are skipped until their cooldown ends.

weights.description: Every enabled credential exactly once; integer weights must be positive and must total 100 within each priority group, because a standby group describes what happens after the preferred group is exhausted.

patch.summary: Set preferred endpoints for shared discovered models
